narrative.overview: The interface is the surface you play on. Choosing a sport repaints the real 3D court in place; the room is that court seen from above and split by the net; the phone is your half of it in your hand. Nothing floats over the playing surface that a groundsman could not have painted there. The result has almost no chrome: no elevation, because paint has none, and no cards, because a region of a court is defined by tape. Colour arrives at page scale as whole fields of acrylic green and electric blue that change per sport.
keyCharacteristics: Flat acrylic paint in two saturated fields per sport, divided only by 5 cm tape
Square corners everywhere; the only curve in the system is a ball
Type stencilled onto the surface, not placed on a panel over it
Optic yellow reserved for the live signal
No shadow, no blur, no glass, no glow, anywhere

rules.name: The White Is Tape Rule
rules.body: White on the court green measures 2.28:1 — a fine painted line and unreadable text. White is structural only; type on green is ink at 7.43:1.

rules.name: The Ground Decides The Ink Rule
rules.body: The apron is not one colour: badminton's is green, where white type fails. Each sport carries groundInk and surfaceInk on its CourtLook, exposed as --on-ground and --on-surface.

rules.name: The Live Signal Rule
rules.body: Optic yellow belongs to the ball and the three things its presence implies: the action that starts play, the live commentary, and the marker for where you are standing.

rules.name: Nothing Covers The Court
rules.body: Only the spec ticket and the caption plate are sanctioned on the playing surface. A control that needs contrast goes to the header strip, which is always apron.

dos: Let a whole field of paint carry the colour; change grounds per sport.
Read the ink off the ground you are painting on, not off a global token.
Give a control its own plate or put it on the apron — never lay a plate over the playing surface to win a contrast check.
Theme the browser's own surfaces: selection, caret, focus ring, scrollbars, accent-color, tabular numerals.
Draw progress with transform: scaleX(); these bars are written every frame.
donts: Don't set white type on the court green, at any size.
Don't add a shadow, a blur, a gradient on type, or a rounded card.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading.
Don't spend optic yellow on anything that is not the live signal.
Don't hide a control behind :hover — the design target includes an iPad.
Don't introduce a third tape weight, or a radius that is not a circle.
